question: What do we call the process of contraction of the cell away from the cell wall due to water loss?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasmolysis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plasmolysis** is the process in plant cells where the cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall due to the loss of water through osmosis.
 
• This occurs when the cell is placed in a hypertonic solution, causing water to move out of the cell and resulting in the shrinking of the cell membrane.
 
• It is a reversible process if the cell is placed back into a hypotonic solution where water can re-enter the cell.
 
• Plasmolysis is often used to demonstrate the principles of osmosis in laboratory settings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DE Plasmolysis:**

 
 
• DE plasmolysis is not a correct term in biological context.
 
• It might be a typographical error or confusion with the term "deplasmolysis," which is the reverse process of plasmolysis.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria use sunlight to synthesize nutrients from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• It produces oxygen as a byproduct and is vital for the survival of most life forms on earth.
 
 
 
• **Cytolysis:**
 
 
• Cytolysis is the bursting or rupturing of a cell membrane when the cell takes in excessive water in a hypotonic environment.
 
• This leads to the cell swelling and eventually bursting due to the lack of a rigid cell wall in animal cells.
